column1: # Cross-document claims whose term the target does not contain, triaged and classed.
# Regenerated by gen_doc_claim_propagation.py + this pass (OPUS, 2026-09-14). `+ this pass`
# is the hand adjudication: the tool writes a staging table and the `verdict` column was
# added on top of it, so re-running the tool does NOT overwrite this file.
# Published into the kit 2026-09-14 from Tools/work/OPUS/triage_doc_claims.py.
# Each row is a QUESTION, not a verdict: the claim may be STALE (the target corrected since) or a
# PARAPHRASE the target words differently. This file decides none of them.
# CLASS, added after adjudicating the run:
#   A-NAMES-IT      the term is an ADDRESS or an IDENTIFIER, so the citing page is asserting that
#                   the target NAMES it. Concrete and checkable. These are the real work.
#   B-FORMULATION   the term is an expression, a formula or a phrase the CITING page composed
#                   while citing the target as support. The target expressing the same fact in
#                   other words is not a defect, and most of these are that.
# Already absorbed by check_doc_claims itself and NOT listed here: code punctuation; leading zeros
# in an offset (+0x038 = +0x38); an INTERIOR address whose containing function the target does
# document (citing the instruction and linking the page that explains its function is correct);
# and a bare number too short to be an address. 33 -> 24.
# A normalisation band that drops every non-alphanumeric was measured and REFUSED: it would absorb
# two more rows and also real differences in wording, which is what this check exists to catch.
# VERDICT is filled only where OPUS actually read both documents. Everything else is UNREAD,
# deliberately: a verdict column pre-filled with guesses is inherited as findings.
